function: Generative synthesis of channel impulse responses (digital-twin channel modeling) from measured SISO and 2x2 MIMO data with GAN, WGAN-GP and VAE-WGAN, flattened versus direct Conv3D training (pp. 2-4, 9-10).
system: SISO at 5.9 GHz (20 and 200 km/h); 2x2 MIMO extracted from 4x8 measured data at 2565 MHz; coded OFDM/OCDM, 512 subcarriers, LDPC rate 1/3; no RIS (pp. 4, 15).
method: Generative adversarial learning (unsupervised): GAN, WGAN-GP, VAE-WGAN; MIMO trained either flattened (Linear 2D, PyTorch) or direct (Conv3D, TensorFlow); each model trained separately per dataset (pp. 3-5, 10, 17).
data_channel: Measured CIRs: 5.9 GHz SISO at 20 and 200 km/h [6]; public WIC 2565 MHz, 12,000 samples of 2x2x52; 60 GHz 802.11ad data, results from [40] (pp. 4, 10).
test_conditions: Each model trained and tested on one dataset: SISO Cases A (20 km/h), B (200 km/h), MIMO 1, MIMO 2; no cross-dataset test or data split stated (pp. 4, 10).
baselines: No non-learned channel model. Compared learned generators only: GAN, WGAN-GP, VAE-WGAN, and flattened versus direct training; measured data are the reference (pp. 6-10, 13-15).
metrics: PDF/CDF of path loss, shadow fading, RMS delay spread and PDP; KL, JS and Wasserstein divergences; BER of coded SISO/MIMO OFDM/OCDM; channel capacity; operation counts (pp. 6-17).
complexity: Flattened WGAN-GP O(E*N*D), about 2.5 million ops per epoch; direct Conv3D 10.2 billion (Table 5); per 1000 epochs GAN 1.2e11, WGAN-GP 3.6e11, VAE-WGAN 4.8e11 (pp. 12, 16-17).
openness: No code or data released; trains on the public WIC measured dataset, https://wireless-intelligence.com (p. 17, ref. [28]).
q1_support: p. 4: "This dataset is measured from a real 5G commercial network on a university campus"; p. 4: "The SISO dataset was extracted from the file" of 5.9 GHz measurements [6]. Both are measured CIRs.
q2_support: p. 10: "Case MIMO 1: Training and test from dataset [28]" and "Case MIMO 2: Training and test from dataset [41]"; p. 10: "were retrained using the original" tensor. Each case uses its own data; no model trained on one scenario is tested on another. The BER sweep over 20-400 delay taps (p. 13) is a parameter sweep.
q3_support: p. 2: "a comprehensive evaluation of three deep generative models" (GAN, WGAN-GP, VAE-WGAN) is the whole comparison; measured data are the reference (Figs. 3-22). No non-learned channel model (stochastic, geometry-based or ray-based) is compared.
q4_support: p. 12: "The flattened scheme requires approximately 2.5 million operations"; p. 17, Table 5: per-epoch cost 2,496,000 ops (flattened) and 10,235,904,000 ops (direct); p. 16, Table 4: operations per 1000 epochs for GAN, WGAN-GP, VAE-WGAN.
q5_support: p. 4: "sourced from the publicly available Wireless Intelligence Channel (WIC)" (measured data; link in ref. [28], p. 17). The authors release no code or data of their own.
notes: Include, area 2: GAN-family models synthesize channel impulse responses (synthesis of the channel is part of area 2); the OFDM/OCDM BER and capacity runs only validate the generated channels. OCDM is a waveform used for evaluation, not OTFS, and no learned detector or estimator is used, so area 4 does not apply. The system check is met by the 2x2 MIMO case although SISO is also studied. Case MIMO 2 (4x4, 60 GHz) results are cited from the authors' earlier work [40] (p. 10). q3 is 0 because only learned generators are compared. The text says the direct scheme costs five times more (p. 12) while Table 5 gives about 4,100 times. Tables 1-5 and Figs. 1-3, 17-22 were read from page images.
